claims.text: Optimized heat treatment generates a fine, uniformly distributed nano-precipitate network in Modified 9Cr-1Mo steel.
Conventional heat treatment produces coarser and less uniformly distributed precipitates in Modified 9Cr-1Mo steel.
A refined nano-precipitate network promotes formation of a stable, homogeneous Cr-rich passive film.
Nano-precipitates act as nucleation sites for chromium enrichment in the passive film.
Fine, uniformly distributed nano-precipitates promote homogeneous nucleation and anchoring of a Cr-enriched passive film.
A homogeneous Cr-enriched passive film retards localized anodic dissolution.
Retarding localized anodic dissolution improves corrosion resistance.
Coarse precipitate distributions cause inhomogeneous passivation.
Inhomogeneous passivation increases susceptibility to localized corrosion.
Optimally heat-treated specimens will have 20-40% lower corrosion rates than conventionally treated specimens.
Optimally heat-treated specimens will exhibit higher electrochemical impedance than conventionally treated specimens.
Optimally heat-treated specimens will develop a more uniform and intact Cr-rich passive layer than conventionally treated specimens.
The proposed effects should hold in 1 M sulfuric acid containing chloride ions at ambient temperature.
The proposed effects should hold in deaerated, high-pressure reactor-water chemistry at approximately 300°C and pH about 9.
The predicted effects may not persist outside the specified exposure conditions.
Other microstructural or compositional factors may influence passivation.
